Adding some technical detail from the runtime team side — prefixing answers so they're easy to pick up in the plan:

- Warm pool & scale-up times:
  * Warm pool (pre-warmed model context + GPU warm process) dramatically reduces node onboarding time. For medium-sized chat models we typically see warm-pool attach times of ~15-45s depending on model size and available GPU type.
  * Cold start (no warm pool) can be 90-180s for large models due to model loading and kernel init.
  * Hybrid approach: keep a small dedicated warm pool for interactive tier (sized to handle expected baseline + N short spikes) + autoscaler that can draw from pre-warmed spill nodes.

- Queueing & backpressure behaviour:
  * Our serving runtime uses short FIFO queues per-route with soft backpressure. During sustained overload we apply request prioritization (interactive > batch) and graceful shedding for lowest-priority work.
  * We expose per-request tracing + queue depth metrics so you can see when tail latency is driven by queueing vs compute.

- Burst strategy options:
  * Reserved Dedicated nodes for guaranteed capacity during Black Friday windows (simplest for guaranteed 95p).
  * Warm pool + rapid autoscaling (best-effort with much lower cost) - sizing math: warm_pool_size ~ baseline + 20% buffer for common spikes; for extreme upper-bound spikes we recommend a short reserved burst commit or cross-region fallback.

We can run a perf test with the following knobs: model variant, sequence length distribution, streaming vs non-streaming mode, concurrency pattern, and ramp profile (10x in 2m, hold 15m). I will prepare a short-runbook for the test and include expected observability outputs.

- Action: I'll produce an runbook + expected metrics table and share by EOD tomorrow.
